newsitem.title: USA: US House Democrats want pro-growth Fed nominees.
newsitem.headline: US House Democrats want pro-growth Fed nominees.

text.p: Fifty House Democrats urged President Clinton on Thursday to nominate pro-growth candidates to two empty positions on the Federal Reserve Board.
In a letter to the Democratic president, the group also called on Clinton to tap a minority nominee to the central bank to meet the "pressing need" for diversity there

"We are writing to express our concerns about the two pending nominations to the board," the lawmakers said in their letter. "We strongly believe that any candidates for the board must respect and value the full employment goals of U.S. monetary policy."

Rep. Maurice Hinchey of New York headed the list of signatories. Among those who signed were: House Democratic Whip David Bonior from Michigan, former House Banking Committee Chairman Henry Gonzalez from Texas and Pete Stark from California.

"I am very concerned that the Fed will continue to plod along as it has with its foor on the brake of the economy," Hinchey told Reuters. "There has got to be at the very least another voice on the Fed speaking for the value of stronger economic growth," he added. Hinchey said that the lawmakers had not discussed any specific names of potential candidates.

The two posts on the seven-member Fed board opened up with the departure of Governors Lawrence Lindsey and Janet Yellen. Any Fed nominations would be subject to confirmation by the Republican-controlled Senate.
"Monetary policy is too important for only financial interests to be represented behind the Federal Reserve Board's decision-making process," the lawmakers said.
Noting that no hispanics and only two blacks have ever served on the Fed board, the Democrats urged Clinton to "nominate a minority candidate" to the central bank.
